turns.prompt_text: How can I verify that the 3% points happens at ikea?
turns.response_html:
If you're looking to verify that you are receiving 3% back (or points) on an IKEA purchase, the process depends on which credit card or program you are using. Usually, the "3% at IKEA" confusion stems from how different cards categorize the store.

1. If you have the IKEA® Visa® Credit Card

There is a common misunderstanding with this card:

  • The Store: You actually get 5% back in rewards for IKEA purchases (including TaskRabbit and installation).
  • The 3% Category: The 3% back is reserved for Dining, Groceries, and Utilities.
  • The IKEA Restaurant: If you eat at the IKEA Swedish Restaurant or Bistro, it often codes as "IKEA" (5%), but occasionally it can code as "Dining" (3%) depending on the specific terminal.

How to verify:

  • Log in to Comenity/Bread Financial: Visit the IKEA Visa account portal.
  • Check Transaction Details: Click on a specific IKEA transaction. It should list the "Rewards Earned" or "Category." If it says "Home/Furniture," it’s likely 5%. If it says "Dining," it’s 3%.
  • Monthly Statement: Your monthly PDF statement will have a "Rewards Summary" section that breaks down points earned in the 5%, 3%, and 1% buckets.

2. If you have the Bank of America® Customized Cash Rewards

This card is popular for IKEA because it has a 3% "Home Improvement & Furnishings" category.

  • Verify in App: Open the Bank of America app, tap your card, and select the IKEA transaction.
  • Category Check: Look for the Merchant Category. For the 3% to apply, it must be categorized under "Home Improvement" or "Furniture Stores." IKEA is almost always categorized correctly here.

3. If you are using IKEA Family (Loyalty Program)

IKEA Family is a separate loyalty program (not a credit card). It typically awards 1 point per $1 spent rather than a percentage.

  • Verify in IKEA App: Open the IKEA app, go to your profile, and tap "IKEA Family Rewards."
  • History Tab: You can see a list of recent transactions and the points credited for each. Note that points can take 48–72 hours to appear after a purchase.

4. General Verification (Any Other Card)

If you're using a card like the Venmo Visa (3% on your top category) or a generic "Shopping" card:

  • Merchant Category Code (MCC): Check the transaction in your bank's app. If it is labeled as "Furniture" or "Shopping," it will trigger whichever category your card associates with those tags.

Quick Tip: If you just made the purchase today, you likely won't see the points "pending" as a specific percentage yet. Wait until the transaction posts (usually 2–3 days) to see the final rewards calculation in your banking portal.

turns.prompt_text: I am going to be using my AmEx grocery card.
turns.response_html:
Since you're using an American Express "grocery card"—most likely the Blue Cash Everyday® or Blue Cash Preferred®—there’s a specific catch regarding how IKEA is categorized.

To get 3% back at IKEA with an AmEx card, the transaction typically needs to happen online, as IKEA is not categorized as a "supermarket."

1. The "Online Retail" Loophole

If you have the Blue Cash Everyday (BCE) card, you earn 3% on U.S. Online Retail Purchases.

  • Online/App: If you order through the IKEA website or app for delivery or "Click & Collect," it almost always codes as "Online Retail," triggering the 3%.
  • In-Store: If you swipe your physical card at an IKEA warehouse, AmEx will categorize it as "Furniture" or "Home Furnishings." Since this isn't a supermarket, it will only earn 1%.

2. How to Verify the Rewards

AmEx doesn't show the exact reward percentage until the transaction has fully "posted" (not just pending). Here is how to check:

  • In the AmEx App:
    1. Wait 2–3 days for the transaction to move from "Pending" to your recent activity.
    2. Tap the IKEA transaction.
    3. Look for a section labeled "Category" or "Rewards Earned." 4. If it says "3% (U.S. Online Retail)" or shows a reward amount equal to 3% of the total, you’re good.
  • On the Web Portal:
    1. Log in and go to Statements & Activity.
    2. Click the IKEA transaction to expand the details.
    3. Check the "Merchant Category". If it says "Online Retail," you got the 3%. If it says "Furniture Stores" or "Wholesale," it likely stayed at 1%.

3. Check for AmEx Offers

Before you buy, check the "AmEx Offers" tab in your app. AmEx frequently has offers like "Spend $250+ at IKEA, get $25 back" or "Earn 2 additional points per dollar." * How to Verify: Once you add the offer to your card and make the purchase, AmEx will usually send you an automated email within minutes saying, "Great news! You just used your AmEx Offer."
